title: 176. The Power of DBT: How to Change Your Behaviors & Cultivate Hope feat. Dr. Maddy Ellberger
description_html: Today's guest is Dr. Maddy Ellberger, PhD, LCSW— a licensed clinical social worker and adjunct professor at Columbia University who received her Masters and Doctoral training in Clinical Social Work from Columbia University and New York University. She is the founder of Downtown Behavioral Wellness, a therapeutic practice that utilizes cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), and mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR).

+ Downtown Behavioral Wellness

+ Contact Maddy

+ Cognitive-Behavioral Treatment of Borderline Personality Disorder

+ Building a Life Worth Living: A Memoir
summary: sadie talks with dr. maddy ellberger, a clinical social worker and dbt specialist, about how dialectical behavioral therapy actually works. they break down the difference between cbt and dbt (behavior change vs. thought change), explain marsha linehan's story and why she created dbt for people who feel misunderstood and out of control emotionally, and walk through the practical tools—diary cards, parent involvement for teens, and the role of invalidating environments. maddy explains why dbt asks you to change what you do, not who you are, and what to do when you feel hopeless about therapy working. listeners learn what makes dbt different, who it's for, and how mindfulness underpins everything.
